headline: Funding flows. Defense budgets swell. Satellites multiply.
deck: This week saw significant investments in space and defense sectors, highlighting a growing appetite for satellite technology.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The funding will bolster its efforts in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, appealing to the Department of Defense's increasing focus on space vulnerabilities. With DoD pull-through now in full effect, the company is positioning itself as a key player in a sector that is only becoming more crucial.
stories.soWhat: Investors seem to believe that space security is the new gold rush, even if the 'innovation' is just repackaged surveillance.

stories.head: L3Harris and Sierra Space score $1.75B missile-tracking deal
stories.body: L3Harris and Sierra Space have been awarded a hefty $1.75 billion contract to build 36 satellites aimed at enhancing the U.S. missile-tracking network. This deal underscores the rising defense budgets, which are up 12% in Europe and likely to follow suit in the U.S. as geopolitical tensions persist. The partnership is a clear signal that the U.S. is doubling down on its missile defense capabilities.
stories.soWhat: If you thought defense spending was plateauing, think again; the sky's quite literally the limit.

stories.head: U.K. plans new space strategy amid vague aspirations
stories.body: The U.K. government is preparing to unveil a new space strategy, which is expected to be a bureaucratic masterpiece of vague aspirations. While details remain scarce, the emphasis on aligning with commercial space initiatives suggests a desire to keep pace with competitors like the U.S. and China. However, the strategy could easily become another exercise in fluff without concrete commitments or funding.
stories.soWhat: If past strategies are any guide, this might just be a way to fill the airwaves without actually moving the needle.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Flexell Space's $20M Series A
watchlist.body: Investors are still willing to back solar solutions, which might indicate a shift in focus toward sustainable space technologies.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant progresses
watchlist.body: With its critical design review cleared, the Dream Chaser's timeline will be under scrutiny as the DoD variant aims for operational readiness.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension could signal more government contracts
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension may set a precedent for similar extensions as the government continues to seek data solutions.

watchlist.title: Watch for updates on Anduril and L3Harris partnership
watchlist.body: Their tactical SDA constellation bid could reshape how the U.S. approaches space-based defense.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
